caption:
A foundit survey reported by ANI in late July found roughly half of India's professionals already job-hunting through appraisal season. Most of them will carry the same problem across the door.

Being overlooked is rarely an organisation problem. It's a presence problem. If your idea only lands when a louder colleague repeats it, a new logo on your ID card changes nothing. You will walk into the next room with the same hedged voice, the same apologetic posture, the same habit of filling silence before anyone has weighed what you said.

In command, you don't get to pick a better room. You get the room you're in and the bearing you brought to it. Tone. Stillness. Calculated silence. These travel with you — and so does their absence.

Fix the signal before you change the address. Otherwise you're not escaping invisibility. You're relocating it, at a 20% hike.

topic.title: Switching jobs won't fix being unseen
topic.angle: Half of Indian professionals respond to being passed over by job-hunting, but most carry the same invisibility into the next organisation — a contrarian argument that directly contradicts the dominant 'jump for the hike' advice.
topic.why_now: A foundit survey reported by ANI in late July found around half of India's professionals already job-hunting during appraisal season, making this live for anyone inside or approaching an appraisal or mid-year review window.
